properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding
expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM Tuesday to 1 PM PST
Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the
time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7
AM on Monday to 10 AM on Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak Tuesday through Wednesday,
reaching 7.9-8.3 feet, likely re-breaking the all-time tidal
records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the
tides will remain around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, but an
incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday will bring a sharp
increase to the surf by Thursday morning's high tide. Breaking
waves may reach 6-8 feet with sets up to 10 feet on west-facing
beaches. Surf then moderates some into Friday, but still looks
to be around 5-8 feet.

* WHERE...Portions of central and south central Montana, especially

* WHEN...Until 10 AM MST Monday.

properties.areaDesc: Ontonagon; Houghton; Baraga; Southern Houghton
properties.description:
* WHAT...Lake effect snow expected. Total snow accumulations between
2 and 5 inches. Up to 8 inches underneath the dominant lake effect
snow band.

* WHERE...Baraga, Northern Houghton, Ontonagon, and Southern Houghton
Counties.

* WHEN...From 7 PM this evening to 11 AM EST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slippery road conditions. Moderate to heavy
snowfall rates will cause visibility to fall below 1 mile at times.
The hazardous conditions will impact the Monday morning commute.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A dominant lake effect band with heavy
snowfall rates up to 1 inch per hour at times will yield an area of
6-8 inches of snow. Medium confidence in exact placement of this
band. Area of focus is between Ontonagon, Painesdale, Herman,
Covington, and Bruce Crossing. Heaviest snowfall expected to remain
south of Houghton.
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 22 at 2:09PM EST until November 23 at 11:00AM EST by NWS Marquette MI
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling.

During lake effect snow, the weather can vary from bands of locally
heavy snow to dry weather just a few miles away. Visibilities can
also vary greatly. Be prepared for rapid changes in weather,
visibility, and road conditions.

Bayamon...Catano...Guaynabo and Toa Baja...

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.description:
ESFSEW

A series of progressive systems will bring rain to western Washington
starting Tuesday and continuing into the weekend. The heaviest
rainfall is expected late Wednesday into Thursday, with rainfall
amounts over the Olympics ranging generally between 2 to 3 inches.
This will lead to rises on the Skokomish River in Mason County late
Wednesday into Thursday. Flooding will be possible starting midweek
and continuing into the weekend.

Please monitor the latest river forecasts from the National Weather
Service for additional information.
